# DropdownMenu

Generated from the spec. This page is a reference to the contract, not usage guidance.

A button that opens a list of actions or choices. Use it for commands and settings, not for site navigation or for picking a form value.

Stage: **alpha**. Figma: `Dropdown` (mapping not yet confirmed against the Components file). Behaviour: `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu`.

A compound component: each part with an element is exported as its own component (DropdownMenu<Part>), and a prop keyed `part.prop` is a prop of that part's component. Parts whose element is null render nothing of their own.

## Anatomy

| Part | data-slot | Element | Kind | Role | Wraps | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| root | `dropdown-menu` | none (renders nothing) | slot |  | `DropdownMenu.Root` | Holds the open state and wires the trigger to the content. It renders no element of its own, so no element in the page carries data-slot="dropdown-menu"; the slot value is reserved for it. It takes no styles and no states. |
| trigger | `dropdown-menu-trigger` | `button` | control | menubutton | `DropdownMenu.Trigger` | The button that opens and closes the menu. Usually a Souvenir Button passed with asChild, which keeps its own look; this spec gives the trigger no styles of its own. |
| portal | `dropdown-menu-portal` | none (renders nothing) | slot |  | `DropdownMenu.Portal` | Moves the content to the end of the body so that no parent's overflow or stacking can clip it. It renders no element of its own and takes no styles and no states. |
| content | `dropdown-menu-content` | `div` | container | menu | `DropdownMenu.Content` | The floating list: Figma's Dropdown. It is placed next to the trigger, flips to the other side when there is no room, and is named by the trigger. |
| group (optional) | `dropdown-menu-group` | `div` | container | group | `DropdownMenu.Group` | A set of related items under one label. |
| label (optional) | `dropdown-menu-label` | `div` | container | grouplabel | `DropdownMenu.Label` | The heading of a group. It is not focusable and cannot be chosen. It is a container rather than a text part because it needs padding to line up with the item text. |
| item (optional) | `dropdown-menu-item` | `div` | control | menuitem | `DropdownMenu.Item` | One action: Figma's DropdownItem. Choosing it runs the action and closes the menu. |
| checkboxItem (optional) | `dropdown-menu-checkbox-item` | `div` | control | menuitemcheckbox | `DropdownMenu.CheckboxItem` | A setting that is on or off, independent of the others. Figma draws it as a DropdownItem in its selected state when on. |
| radioGroup (optional) | `dropdown-menu-radio-group` | `div` | container | group | `DropdownMenu.RadioGroup` | A set of radio items of which exactly one is chosen. |
| radioItem (optional) | `dropdown-menu-radio-item` | `div` | control | menuitemradio | `DropdownMenu.RadioItem` | One of several exclusive choices inside a radio group. Figma draws the chosen one as a DropdownItem in its selected state. |
| indicatorBox (optional) | `dropdown-menu-indicator-box` | `span` | container |  |  | A fixed-width box at the start of every checkbox and radio item. It is always present, so the label does not move sideways when the item is checked or unchecked. |
| itemIndicator (optional) | `dropdown-menu-item-indicator` | `span` | glyph | indicator | `DropdownMenu.ItemIndicator` | The check mark or dot inside the indicator box. Radix mounts it only while the item is checked. Hidden from assistive technology; aria-checked on the item says the same thing. |
| iconStart (optional) | `dropdown-menu-icon-start` | `span` | glyph | indicator |  | An optional icon before the label of an action item. Figma's prefix. Hidden from assistive technology. |
| itemLabel | `dropdown-menu-item-label` | `span` | text |  |  | The words of any item kind: Figma's title. They are the item's accessible name and its type-ahead text. A long label wraps. |
| itemDescription (optional) | `dropdown-menu-item-description` | `span` | text |  |  | An optional second line under the label of any item kind: Figma's description. It is the item's accessible description, never part of its name or its type-ahead text. |
| iconEnd (optional) | `dropdown-menu-icon-end` | `span` | glyph | indicator |  | An optional icon after the label of an action item. Figma's suffix. Hidden from assistive technology. |
| itemShortcut (optional) | `dropdown-menu-item-shortcut` | `span` | text |  |  | An optional keyboard shortcut hint at the end of an action item, such as ⌘C. Hidden from assistive technology; the item carries the same shortcut in aria-keyshortcuts, written as key names joined by + (Meta+C for ⌘C), so it is not read as part of the name. |
| separator (optional) | `dropdown-menu-separator` | `div` | layer | separator | `DropdownMenu.Separator` | A horizontal line between groups, one Border width/sm thick. Not focusable. |

## Keyboard

Pattern: [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: Menu Button, opening a Menu](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/). Name: The trigger: its label, or with an icon-only Button its ariaLabel. The content is named by the trigger through aria-labelledby, which Radix sets. Each item is named by its label alone; an item with a description is labelled by its itemLabel and described by its itemDescription, which the adapter links. Each group and radio group is named by its label through aria-labelledby, which the adapter sets because Radix's Label is a plain div with no link to its group.

| Key | Part | Does | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | trigger | Opens the menu and highlights the first enabled item; on an open menu's trigger it closes the menu. | `dropdown-menu-trigger-enter-opens` |
| Space | trigger | Same as Enter. | `dropdown-menu-trigger-space-opens` |
| ArrowDown | trigger | Opens the menu and highlights the first enabled item. ArrowUp on the trigger does nothing; the menu-button pattern lists it as optional and Radix leaves it out. | `dropdown-menu-trigger-arrowdown-opens` |
| ArrowDown | content | Highlights the next enabled item. On the last item it stays put unless content.loop is true. With focus on the content itself, after a pointer open, it highlights the first enabled item. | `dropdown-menu-arrowdown-next` |
| ArrowUp | content | Highlights the previous enabled item. On the first item it stays put unless content.loop is true. With focus on the content itself it highlights the last enabled item. | `dropdown-menu-arrowup-previous` |
| Home | content | Highlights the first enabled item. PageUp does the same. | `dropdown-menu-home-first` |
| End | content | Highlights the last enabled item. PageDown does the same. | `dropdown-menu-end-last` |
| Enter | item | Chooses the highlighted item: runs its action, toggles a checkbox item or picks a radio item, then closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. | `dropdown-menu-enter-selects` |
| Space | item | Same as Enter, including on checkbox and radio items, where the pattern would keep the menu open. While a type-ahead search is in progress, Space is part of the search instead. | `dropdown-menu-space-selects` |
| Escape | content | Closes the menu without choosing anything and returns focus to the trigger. | `dropdown-menu-escape-closes` |
| Tab | content | Does nothing: Radix cancels it and focus stays on the highlighted item. The pattern says Tab closes the menu and moves on; Souvenir keeps Radix's behaviour. | `dropdown-menu-tab-held` |
| type-ahead | content | Typing printable characters highlights the next enabled item whose label starts with them. Typed characters build one search for one second. Repeating a single letter steps through the items that start with it. | `dropdown-menu-type-ahead` |

## Requirements

Grouped MUST, then SHOULD, then COULD. A check starting manual: is not proven by a machine.

| Level | Id | Requirement | Checked by | WCAG |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-trigger-attributes` | The trigger has aria-haspopup set to menu, aria-expanded set to true or false to match the menu, and aria-controls naming the content while it is open. | `test:dropdown-menu-trigger-attributes` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-trigger-one-button` | With a Button as trigger, asChild is set, so the page holds one button element and never a button inside a button. | `axe:nested-interactive` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-content-named` | The content has role menu and aria-labelledby pointing at the trigger's id. | `test:dropdown-menu-content-named` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-structure` | The content and every group in it hold only menu items, groups and separators as their owned children. | `axe:aria-required-children` | 1.3.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-item-parent` | Every menu item, checkbox item and radio item sits inside the content or a group inside it. | `axe:aria-required-parent` | 1.3.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-item-name` | Every action item has an accessible name from its label. | `axe:aria-command-name` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-toggle-item-name` | Every checkbox and radio item has an accessible name from its label. | `axe:aria-toggle-field-name` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-description-not-name` | An item of any kind with a description has aria-labelledby pointing at its itemLabel and aria-describedby pointing at its itemDescription, so its accessible name is the label alone; type-ahead matches the label and never the description. | `test:dropdown-menu-description-not-name` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-group-labelled` | A group or radio group that has a label carries aria-labelledby pointing at that label's id. The adapter sets both ids, because Radix does not. | `test:dropdown-menu-group-labelled` | 1.3.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-checked-state` | aria-checked on every checkbox and radio item matches its checked value, and exactly one radio item in a radio group with a value is checked. | `test:dropdown-menu-checked-state` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-glyphs-hidden` | The item indicator, iconStart, iconEnd and the shortcut hint carry aria-hidden. | `test:dropdown-menu-glyphs-hidden` | 1.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-trigger-enter-opens` | Enter on the closed trigger opens the menu with the first enabled item highlighted and focused. | `test:dropdown-menu-trigger-enter-opens` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-trigger-space-opens` | Space on the closed trigger opens the menu with the first enabled item highlighted and focused. | `test:dropdown-menu-trigger-space-opens` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-trigger-arrowdown-opens` | ArrowDown on the closed trigger opens the menu with the first enabled item highlighted and focused. | `test:dropdown-menu-trigger-arrowdown-opens` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-arrowdown-next` | ArrowDown moves the highlight to the next enabled item, skips disabled items, and stays on the last item while content.loop is false. | `test:dropdown-menu-arrowdown-next` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-arrowup-previous` | ArrowUp moves the highlight to the previous enabled item, skips disabled items, and stays on the first item while content.loop is false. | `test:dropdown-menu-arrowup-previous` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-home-first` | Home and PageUp move the highlight to the first enabled item. | `test:dropdown-menu-home-first` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-end-last` | End and PageDown move the highlight to the last enabled item. | `test:dropdown-menu-end-last` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-enter-selects` | Enter on a highlighted item calls its handler once, closes the menu and focuses the trigger. | `test:dropdown-menu-enter-selects` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-space-selects` | Space on a highlighted item calls its handler once, closes the menu and focuses the trigger. | `test:dropdown-menu-space-selects` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-escape-closes` | Escape closes the menu without calling any item's handler and focuses the trigger. | `test:dropdown-menu-escape-closes` | 2.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-tab-held` | Tab inside the open menu leaves focus on the highlighted item and the menu open, as Radix does. A change to close on Tab, as the pattern describes, must change this test first. | `test:dropdown-menu-tab-held` | 2.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-type-ahead` | Typing the first letters of an enabled item's label highlights it; disabled items are never matched. | `test:dropdown-menu-type-ahead` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-focus-returns` | After the menu closes by Escape or by choosing an item, focus is on the trigger. | `test:dropdown-menu-focus-returns` | 2.4.3 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-pointer-open-focus` | Opened by pointer, focus is on the content and no item has data-highlighted until the mouse moves over one or an arrow key is pressed. | `test:dropdown-menu-pointer-open-focus` | 2.4.3 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-disabled-inert` | A disabled item has aria-disabled true, cannot be highlighted by arrow keys, type-ahead or the mouse, and pressing it calls no handler and leaves the menu open. | `test:dropdown-menu-disabled-inert` |  |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-highlight-one-look` | An item highlighted by the mouse and the same item highlighted by ArrowDown have the same computed background and text colour, and no item stylesheet rule uses :hover. | `test:dropdown-menu-highlight-one-look` |  |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-no-hover-selector` | The generated stylesheet styles item highlight only through [data-highlighted], never through :hover or :focus. | `lint:no-hover-on-menu-items` |  |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-highlight-visible` | The highlighted item's background has at least 3 to 1 contrast against the content's background, in every variant, in light and dark. | `test:dropdown-menu-highlight-visible` | 1.4.11 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-highlight-not-colour-alone` | The highlight never relies on colour alone: the highlighted item gains a filled block behind its whole width whose lightness differs from the content by at least 3 to 1, its text inverts against that fill, and with forced colours on an outline replaces the fill. A checked checkbox or radio item shows its check mark or dot, never only a colour. | `test:dropdown-menu-highlight-not-colour-alone` | 1.4.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-text-contrast` | Every label, description, group label and shortcut hint has at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against its background, highlighted or not, in every variant, in light and dark. Disabled items are exempt. | `test:dropdown-menu-text-contrast` | 1.4.3 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-forced-colors-highlight` | With forced colours on, the highlighted item shows an outline at least 2 pixels thick and the others show none. | `test:dropdown-menu-forced-colors-highlight` | 2.4.7 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-target-size` | Every item is at least 24 pixels tall and as wide as the content. | `test:dropdown-menu-target-size` | 2.5.8 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-item-layout` | Each item lays out in one row, in reading order: the indicator box or iconStart, then a column holding the label with the description under it, then iconEnd, then the shortcut hint at the end edge. The label column takes the remaining width, the icons and indicator box never shrink, and the shortcut does not wrap. The extensions stylesheet writes this. | `test:dropdown-menu-item-layout` | 1.3.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-label-wraps` | A label or description too long for one line wraps inside the item, which grows taller and keeps its padding; it is never cut off or hidden behind the shortcut. | `test:dropdown-menu-label-wraps` | 1.4.10 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-separator-line` | The separator is one line, 1 pixel (width/sm) thick, in border/primary/default, across the content's inner width, drawn on its block-start edge only, with space above and below it. The extensions stylesheet writes the one-sided border, the zero height and the space. | `test:dropdown-menu-separator-line` |  |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-fits-viewport` | At 320 pixels wide the open content lies wholly inside the viewport, at least content.collisionPadding from each edge, and no page scrolls sideways. Because menu/max (320) is wider than the 304 pixels left inside the padding, the extensions stylesheet also caps the width at --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-width. | `test:dropdown-menu-fits-viewport` | 1.4.10 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-scrolls-when-tall` | Content taller than the space Radix reports as available is capped at that height and scrolls inside itself, so every item can be reached on a short phone screen. The extensions stylesheet sets the maximum height from --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height and the vertical overflow. | `test:dropdown-menu-scrolls-when-tall` | 1.4.10 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-modal-blocks-page` | While open with modal true, the rest of the page is hidden from assistive technology, does not scroll and ignores presses; a press outside closes the menu. | `test:dropdown-menu-modal-blocks-page` |  |
| SHOULD | `dropdown-menu-shortcut-exposed` | An item with a shortcut hint carries the same shortcut in aria-keyshortcuts, written as key names joined by + (Meta+C for the hint ⌘C), never as the glyphs of the hint. | `test:dropdown-menu-shortcut-exposed` |  |
| SHOULD | `dropdown-menu-touch-target` | Where the pointer is coarse every item is at least 44 pixels tall. (pattern) | `test:dropdown-menu-touch-target` |  |
| SHOULD | `dropdown-menu-danger-not-colour-alone` | An item with variant danger names what it destroys in its label, such as Delete chat, because red alone does not tell everyone that the action is destructive. (pattern) | `manual:dropdown-menu-danger-not-colour-alone` | 1.4.1 |
| SHOULD | `dropdown-menu-right-item-kind` | A choice of one from several uses a radio group, an independent on or off setting uses a checkbox item, and only commands use plain items, so the checked state is announced. (pattern) | `manual:dropdown-menu-right-item-kind` | 4.1.2 |
| COULD | `dropdown-menu-trigger-shows-open` | The trigger's chevron icon points up while the menu is open and down while it is closed, chosen from aria-expanded, as the model selector fixes ask. People may read the flipped chevron as a sign the menu can be closed again. (assumption) | `manual:dropdown-menu-trigger-shows-open` |  |
| COULD | `dropdown-menu-short-groups` | A group holds about seven items or fewer, on the belief that people scan a short menu faster than a long one; a longer list of choices belongs in a list or a dialog. (assumption) | `manual:dropdown-menu-short-groups` |  |
| COULD | `dropdown-menu-checkbox-stays-open` | A checkbox item could keep the menu open when chosen, by calling preventDefault in onSelect, so several settings can be changed in one visit. Whether people expect this in Souvenir's menus is untested. (assumption) | `manual:dropdown-menu-checkbox-stays-open` |  |

## Content rules

- Item labels are short and start with a verb for actions: Rename chat, not Chat renaming.
- Checkbox and radio item labels name the setting or the choice, not the act of choosing: Extended thinking, Standard.
- A description is one short sentence that adds what the label cannot, such as Best for long documents. Leave it out when the label says enough.
- Group labels are short nouns, such as Models. Leave a label out when the items speak for themselves.
- Sentence case. No full stop in labels. An ellipsis only when the item opens a further step that asks for more, such as Rename….
- A danger item names what it destroys and sits last, after a separator.
- Shortcut hints use the platform's symbols, such as ⌘C on Apple devices and Ctrl+C elsewhere, and only for shortcuts that work.

## Style rules

Every rule of the spec, in order. The generated stylesheet keeps this order and gives every rule for a part the same specificity, so a later rule wins where two set the same property.

| Rule | When | Parts and declarations | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| styles[0] | always | content: background surface/primary/default, borderColor border/strong/default, borderWidth width/sm, borderStyle solid, radius container/medium, shadow shadow/md, minWidth menu/min, maxWidth menu/max, paddingBlock static/40, paddingInline static/40<br>label: paddingInline static/80, paddingBlock static/60, typography label-base, color text/secondary<br>item: minHeight control/sm, paddingInline static/80, paddingBlock static/60, gap static/80, radius container/small, background transparent, color text/primary, typography body-base, cursor default, outlineWidth none<br>checkboxItem: minHeight control/sm, paddingInline static/80, paddingBlock static/60, gap static/80, radius container/small, background transparent, color text/primary, typography body-base, cursor default, outlineWidth none<br>radioItem: minHeight control/sm, paddingInline static/80, paddingBlock static/60, gap static/80, radius container/small, background transparent, color text/primary, typography body-base, cursor default, outlineWidth none<br>indicatorBox: width icon/sm, height icon/sm<br>itemIndicator: iconSize icon/sm, color current<br>iconStart: iconSize icon/sm, color current<br>iconEnd: iconSize icon/sm, color current<br>itemLabel: color inherit<br>itemDescription: color text/secondary, typography body-small<br>itemShortcut: color text/secondary, typography body-small<br>separator: borderColor border/primary/default, borderWidth width/sm | The content is a floating surface, not a divider, so its edge is border/strong/default: in the dark theme shadow/md barely shows and the edge has to hold the menu apart from the page. border/primary/default is kept for the separator, which is a divider. Items are 32 pixels tall: 6 pixels of padding above and below a 20 pixel line. The separator takes its colour and its width/sm thickness here; the extensions stylesheet draws it on the block-start edge only, with no height, so the line is 1 pixel. |
| styles[1] | states itemHighlighted | item: background interactive/neutral/default, color text/inverse<br>itemShortcut: color current<br>itemDescription: color current | The highlight is the only sign of keyboard focus in a menu, so it must be seen, and it is a filled block with inverted text rather than a change of hue: interactive/neutral/default is 21 to 1 against the content in light and 17.6 to 1 in dark. The subtle fills fail: surface/primary/hover is 1.06 to 1 and surface/tertiary/default 1.13 to 1 in light. The description and shortcut follow the inverted text, because text/secondary on the dark fill would fail. |
| styles[2] | states checkboxItemHighlighted | checkboxItem: background interactive/neutral/default, color text/inverse<br>itemDescription: color current |  |
| styles[3] | states radioItemHighlighted | radioItem: background interactive/neutral/default, color text/inverse<br>itemDescription: color current |  |
| styles[4] | props {"item.variant":"danger"} | item: color text/error | text/error is 4.83 to 1 on the content in light and 6.36 to 1 in dark. The icons follow it through current. |
| styles[5] | props {"item.variant":"danger"}; states itemHighlighted | item: background interactive/error/default, color text/on<br>itemShortcut: color current<br>itemDescription: color current | text/on on interactive/error/default is 4.83 to 1 in both themes; the fill is 4.83 to 1 against the content in light and 3.65 to 1 in dark. |
| styles[6] | media coarse-pointer | item: minHeight target/min<br>checkboxItem: minHeight target/min<br>radioItem: minHeight target/min | On a touch screen every item is at least 44 pixels tall. |
| styles[7] | states itemHighlighted; media forced-colors | item: outlineColor border/focus, outlineWidth ring/width, outlineOffset none | Forced colours remove background fills, so in that mode the highlight is drawn as an outline with no offset. The 4 pixel padding of the content leaves room for it. |
| styles[8] | states checkboxItemHighlighted; media forced-colors | checkboxItem: outlineColor border/focus, outlineWidth ring/width, outlineOffset none |  |
| styles[9] | states radioItemHighlighted; media forced-colors | radioItem: outlineColor border/focus, outlineWidth ring/width, outlineOffset none |  |
| styles[10] | states itemDisabled | item: background transparent, color text/disabled, cursor not-allowed<br>itemShortcut: color text/disabled<br>itemDescription: color text/disabled | One disabled look for every variant, so a disabled danger item does not still look dangerous. |
| styles[11] | states checkboxItemDisabled | checkboxItem: background transparent, color text/disabled, cursor not-allowed<br>itemDescription: color text/disabled |  |
| styles[12] | states radioItemDisabled | radioItem: background transparent, color text/disabled, cursor not-allowed<br>itemDescription: color text/disabled |  |

## What the spec does not carry

- The live Figma components: their properties were read from a cached copy inside the Semantic Tokens file, which is older than the published library, so every figma mapping here is unconfirmed. In that copy Dropdown, the menu surface, is a plain component with the booleans showGroups and showDivider and no state property; both booleans are design-tool switches with no prop in code. DropdownItem has state (default, hover, selected, focus, disabled; default default), type (initial, danger; default initial), the text properties title and description, and the instance swaps prefix and suffix with the switches showPrefix and showSuffix, which have no prop in code. Figma's hover and focus are one state in code, [data-highlighted]; selected is [data-state="checked"] on a checkbox or radio item.
- The word for a destructive action differs: the Figma property is type with the value danger, and the tokens are the error tokens. The prop follows Figma's value under the name item.variant, because type means the element type in code; the styles use text/error, interactive/error/default and text/on.
- Layout written in the extensions stylesheet: the item as one row (indicator box or iconStart, a label column with the description under the label, iconEnd, then the shortcut pinned to the end edge), with the label column growing and the icons and indicator box not shrinking; white-space nowrap on the shortcut; the content's maximum height from --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height with vertical overflow auto; the content's width capped at --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-width; the separator as a block-start border only, with no height and space above and below it. The requirements dropdown-menu-item-layout, dropdown-menu-separator-line, dropdown-menu-fits-viewport and dropdown-menu-scrolls-when-tall pin each of these.
- Submenus: Radix's Sub, SubTrigger and SubContent are left out. A menu that needs a second level should become a dialog or a page.
- Radix's Arrow part, which points at the trigger.
- Context menus opened by right-click, which are a different Radix package.
- The indeterminate checked state that Radix accepts for checkbox items.
- Icons and shortcut hints on checkbox and radio items: their start is the indicator box, and Figma's prefix and suffix are read here as belonging to action items.
- Any Radix Content prop not listed here, such as alignOffset, avoidCollisions, sticky and hideWhenDetached; they pass through unchanged at Radix's defaults.
- Enter and exit animation. Radix keeps the content mounted with data-state closed while an animation runs, but the spec format has no opacity or transform token, so none is specified.
- The trigger's look, which belongs to the Button spec, including how the chevron turns.
- The rest of the model selector fixes in the UI fixes tracker, such as how the Effort setting works.
